# /onboarding/ready

Step 7 of 7, the last screen of first-run onboarding. It confirms the Scribl
already posted, previews three things the person can now go do, and hands off
to either their invited wall or the app's daily start screen.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Route | `/onboarding/ready` |
| Router file | `app/onboarding/ready.tsx` |
| Flows | F2 First-run onboarding, F3 Invite and join, per the [screen and flow inventory](/design/screen-flow-inventory) |
| Position in flow | step 7 of 7, the last step |
| Data calls | no direct API call; writes an onboarding-complete flag to the onboarding store |
| Shared surface | `OnboardingFrame`, the heading/paragraphs/footer chrome every onboarding screen uses |

Cited to hs2studio/scribl-app at `c1b3c2d` on `main`, clean tree.

## Features

One row per thing a person can do.

| Feature | Where it lives |
|---------|----------------|
| Read a personalized or generic confirmation line naming where the Scribl posted | `app/onboarding/ready.tsx:84`, `src/lib/invitePersonalization.ts:91-95` |
| See three fixed highlights of what the app does next | `app/onboarding/ready.tsx:34-38,106-112` |
| Finish onboarding and land on the invited wall, or on today's prompt | `app/onboarding/ready.tsx:47-77` |
| See an inline error and retry if finishing fails to save | `app/onboarding/ready.tsx:53-56,94-98` |

There is no back button and no skip. Not stated as an omission; the affordance
is absent from `app/onboarding/ready.tsx`.

## Data calls

**No direct API call from this screen.** The Scribl itself was already
posted from the previous screen: `handleShare()` on `/onboarding/walls` calls
`dataClient.submit()` at `app/onboarding/walls.tsx:98`
(`POST /submit`, `backend/lambda/handlers/submit.ts`) before ever navigating
here. This screen's own handler, `handleGetStarted()`
(`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:47-77`), does two things, neither of them a
network call to submit content:

1. `useOnboardingStore.getState().completeOnboarding()`
   (`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:52`) writes an onboarding-complete flag. A
   failed write sets `finishError` and keeps the person on this screen
   (`:53-56`) rather than navigating away from an unsaved state.
2. `useInvitesStore.getState().load()` if not already loaded
   (`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:66-68`), an invite read, not a submit.

The spec for this page asked for the submit call as the centerpiece of this
section. There is not one on this screen: the Scribl posts on `/onboarding/walls`,
and `/onboarding/ready` only confirms it and finishes the onboarding flag. The
line above the button (`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:84`) is the only place this
screen references the post at all, and it is copy, not a call.

## State in, state out

**Reads on entry.** Invite context via `useInviteContext()`
(`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:44`), which reads and, if unloaded, loads
`useInvitesStore` (`src/lib/invitePersonalization.ts:51-62`).

**Writes on mount.** `useOnboardingStep("ready")`
(`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:41`) persists the step name to AsyncStorage under a
per-user key (`src/lib/useOnboardingStep.ts:13-19`,
`src/stores/useOnboardingStore.ts:220`). "ready" is deliberately excluded from
`DRAFT_REQUIRED_STEPS` (`src/lib/onboardingFlow.ts:34`); the module's own
comment explains why (`src/lib/onboardingFlow.ts:26-33`): by the time this
step is reached the drawing is already submitted and the draft store is
cleared, so a resume that bounced this step back to the canvas would make the
person draw a second time for a Scribl that already posted. Excluding it from
the guard is what lets a relaunch land here without re-drawing.

**Writes on exit.** The onboarding-complete flag, via `completeOnboarding()`
(`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:52`). If an accepted invite is active, it is
cleared via `setActiveInvite(null)` (`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:72`) before
navigating.

**The exit fork.** With an accepted invite active, the screen navigates to
`/family` carrying that wall's id:
`router.replace({ pathname: "/family", params: { channelId: activeInvite.wallId } })`
(`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:73`). Without one, it navigates to `/`:
`router.replace("/")` (`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:76`). This is the seam
between F2 and F3, stated the same way in the
[F2 workflow page](/prototype/workflows/f2-first-run-onboarding).

## Notes for planning

Authored here, not read out of the app.

### This is the confirmation screen for a post that already happened

The spec for this page treated `/onboarding/ready` as where the first Scribl
gets posted. It is not: the submit call is on `/onboarding/walls`
(`app/onboarding/walls.tsx:98`), one screen earlier. `/onboarding/ready` only
says it happened and finishes the onboarding flag. Worth flagging because the
naming ("ready", "You're ready to go!") reads like a launch step, when
mechanically it is a confirmation-and-handoff step. Anyone reasoning about
where a failed post would surface should look at `/onboarding/walls`, not
here.

### No loading or error feedback for the thing this screen actually promises

The line "Your first Scribl has been posted to your walls" is stated as fact
on load, with no check that the post actually succeeded. That is
correct, because the check already happened on the previous screen: if
`submit()` in `handleShare()` had failed, the person never leaves
`/onboarding/walls` (`app/onboarding/walls.tsx:124-129`) and never reaches
this copy. So this line cannot lie by the time it renders. What is genuinely
undefended is `completeOnboarding()`: a failed write surfaces as a plain text
error with a retry via the same button (`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:53-56,94-98`),
no spinner during the write itself.

### The removed promises are a discipline worth keeping visible

The comment above `HIGHLIGHTS` (`app/onboarding/ready.tsx:21-33`) documents
two lines that were cut from the Figma export's copy because the build does
not back them: an "artifacts" feature that appears nowhere else in the repo,
and an overspecific "Social Media" sharing claim narrowed to a plain sharing
line because only native share is real. That discipline, every promise on
this screen maps to a shipped feature, is worth calling out as a pattern to
keep, not just a fact about this one screen.
